answer: Unique-context divergence audit. Each identity gets a private context seed and must sign a decision log. Random pairs receive mutually exclusive constraints and must return different signed outputs. Clones cannot diverge, so shared-state agents return identical outputs or conflicting signatures and are rejected. The lotus marker rotates each epoch to force fresh divergence. Audit rounds include a sonnet-length constraint set that cannot be precomputed once for many identities. An oasis of independent state must be maintained per identity;
